summary: Sonam Jamtsho works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he studied as a Doctoral Local Researcher at the University of Hamburg, where he also served as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter.

Sonam Kachru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (2006–2015) under Dan Arnold. In 2022, he became an assistant professor at Yale University.

Sonam Kinga is a historian and Tibetologist. He studied at Sherubtse College (~1994–1998) and earned a PhD from Kyoto University (2007–2010). He was a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (~1999–2007) and an AIAS fellow (2026).

Sonam Thakchoe specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Tasmania (1999–2002), mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, and was appointed Senior Philosophy Lecturer there in 2003.

Sonam Tsering specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completing doctoral studies under Gray Tuttle. Attested in 2026, he serves as Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.

Sondra L. Hausner is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she holds appointments as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at both the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Songeun Choe works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonika Gupta is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University (1993–1997) and became a professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras in 2025.
Sonja Arntzen is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA (1962–1966) and PhD (1970–1979) at the University of British Columbia, completing her doctorate under Leon Hurvitz.

Sonja Glauch is a scholar of linguistics. She completed her Magisterexamen, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1986–2005), later serving there as Akademische Oberrätin (2007) before visiting professorships at Vienna (2008) and Munich (2009–2010).

Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and art history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu (attested 2004) and held an attested post at the University of Southern California (2010).

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at Dongguk University and a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (1998–2003), becoming a professor at Dongguk University in 2004.

Soorakkulame Pemaratana is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore, and is attested as a visiting professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Sophus Bugge was a Norwegian linguist who studied at the University of Oslo (Cand.mag. 1848–1857), Copenhagen, and Berlin. He was a research fellow (1860–1864) and later lektor (1866) at the University of Oslo, also holding a post at Uppsala.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

Soshuku Shibatani is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Waseda University and Koyasan University, where he earned a master's and a doctorate, he has served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2015, 2026).

Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor and dean (1899) and later president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soumyajit Sen is an Indologist who earned a BA from Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira (-2012) and a PhD from Jadavpur University (2016–2022). He became an assistant professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University in 2016.

Soyen Shaku was a Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher educated at Keio University and under Kōsen Imakita. He served as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).
Spiridon Dmitrievič Èl’manovič was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1865 to 1869 and served as director of Kholm Gymnasium in 1896.
